title: Interpretability Driven Evolutionary Approach for the Design of Biological Sequences
claim: Guide mutations of a sequence with an explainable model's critical motifs, then evaluate and update the dataset in an active-learning loop.
layout: 3 rounded panels, left-to-right, big block arrows between stages, nested sub-modules
description: A horizontal three-stage pipeline in rounded containers, joined by large hollow block arrows. On the left, a 'Dataset' panel shows a database cylinder labelled D_{t-1}, a 'Select top B sequences' box, and a smaller cylinder D^top. The large middle panel, 'Interpretable Mutations', starts with a box 'Train Explainable Model on D_{t-1}: ŷ = g(x,Θ)'. It then branches into two paths. The upper path extracts motifs from D^top as colored token strips ranked by attribution score, giving a replacement motif s. The lower path computes attribution scores Φ for x in D^top and picks the position to mutate j. Both paths feed a box of mutated sequences D_M^top. The right panel, 'Evaluate and Update', shows a microscope for the oracle function y = f(x) and an updated database D_t = D_{t-1} ∪ D_M^top. Headings are brown. Sequence strips use orange-to-green heat colors on a gray-white background.
caption: The active learning process of IDEAS. At iteration t, the top-B sequences from Dt−1 form Dtop. An explainable model g(θ)
abstract: Designing biological sequences such as proteins and DNA for desired properties is challenging due to vast search spaces and limited wet lab evaluation budgets. Current evolutionary approaches ignore sequential dependencies and rely on random mutations, which scale poorly for long sequences. In contrast, reinforcement learning (RL) and generative models explicitly model sequence structure but require large datasets to guide generation toward the target properties. These limitations suggest the need for a method that combines the sample efficiency of evolutionary approaches with the ability to exploit sequential structure. In this work, we propose a novel evolutionary approach, $\texttt{IDEAS}$, in which mutations are guided by an explainable model. The model identifies critical motifs in high-fitness sequences and uses them to mutate non-critical positions. Across eight continuous-property datasets, seven baselines, and three evaluation budgets, $\texttt{IDEAS}$ achieves a 19% acceleration in design while maintaining a favorable position on the Pareto curve balancing acceleration, diversity, and novelty.
